entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Minucius Augurinus was a Roman Republican politician of the patrician gens Minucia during the beginning of the 5th century BC. He served as Consul of Rome in 497 BC and 491 BC, both times serving together with Aulus Sempronius Atratinus.

As a prominent figure in the Roman Republic, Augurinus played a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of ancient Rome. His leadership and strategic alliances helped maintain the stability of the Roman state during a time of great turmoil.

Despite his importance, Augurinus's legacy has largely been overlooked in modern historiography. However, his contributions to Roman politics and his involvement in key events of the 5th century BC make him a significant figure in the study of ancient Rome.

The Roman historian Livy, who wrote extensively on the early history of Rome, credited Augurinus with helping to avert a civil war between the patrician and plebeian classes.

As a testament to his enduring influence, the Roman poet and statesman Cicero referenced Augurinus in his own writings, praising his integrity and leadership.

The significance of Marcus Minucius Augurinus lies in his role as a key figure in the Roman Republic, his contributions to the stability of the Roman state, and his lasting impact on Roman politics and historiography.

He was born in 600 BCE and died in 500 BCE.
